summary: The Verge reports that Donald Trump and Republicans are using electric vehicles as a wedge issue to peel working-class autoworkers away from Biden amid the UAW strike. The article argues the attacks are incoherent, since union members are frustrated with both parties and are not opposed to EVs so much as concerned about who builds them and on what terms. It notes that most EV work is non-union, that automakers receive large taxpayer subsidies, and that the transition seems unstoppable.
one_line: Trump and the GOP attack EVs to win over autoworkers during the UAW strike, but workers distrust both parties and want a union-led EV transition.
key_facts: Donald Trump spoke before a crowd in suburban Detroit and called EV advocates "environmental lunatics" while arguing EVs are too expensive, lack range and will cost American jobs.
The United Auto Workers strike had roiled Detroit and the surrounding area for about two weeks, sending candidates from both parties scrambling for worker support.
UAW President Shawn Fain called for a "just transition" to electric cars, and workers are also pushing for higher wages, job security and more manageable hours.
UAW member Aaron Westaway told E&E News: "Nobody's happy with Trump, nobody's happy with Biden."
According to Pew Research, 50 percent of US adults say they are unlikely to buy an EV, while 38 percent said they were likely to consider one.
Ford is building a large battery plant in Tennessee as a joint venture with Korean battery maker SK Innovation.
Workers at a General Motors joint venture battery plant in Ohio overwhelmingly voted to unionize under the UAW late in 2022.
Sydney Ghazarian of the Labor Network for Sustainability said automakers get billions in taxpayer-funded EV subsidies and must not leave workers behind, and called Trump's attacks "faux populism."
As president, Trump appointed anti-union judges and National Labor Relations Board members, and his promises to prevent auto factory shutdowns largely failed.
Joe Biden became the first modern president to visit a picket line, standing with striking UAW members in Wayne County, Michigan, and said they "deserve a significant raise."
The Biden administration is prioritizing billions in federal funding for a robust EV charging network.
Automakers are still losing billions of dollars each year on EVs, and China produces the bulk of EV components, a major union concern.
Trump told autoworkers that "in two years, you're all going to be out of business," and said "The auto industry is being assassinated."
